facts.raw_span: underwent transthoracic echocardiography as part of a routine medical checkup
which revealed a left ventricular mass
A chest radiograph revealed no active lung lesions
Transthoracic echocardiography demonstrated a mobile, smooth, oval, pedunculated mass originating from the left ventricular lateral wall, measuring 1.34 × 1.9 cm
Contrast-enhanced chest computed tomography showed the mass attached to the interventricular septum with focal contrast enhancement

concepts.why: The presence of a mobile, smooth, oval, pedunculated mass originating from the left ventricular lateral wall, as seen on transthoracic echocardiography and contrast-enhanced chest computed tomography, is consistent with a left ventricular myxoma.
The characteristics of the mass, including its mobility, smoothness, and oval shape, could also be consistent with a left ventricular fibroelastoma.

Although less likely given the mass's characteristics, a left ventricular thrombus could still be considered, especially if there were underlying conditions predisposing to thrombosis, though none are mentioned in the vignette.
This rare tumor could present as a mass in the left ventricle, although it is more commonly associated with tuberous sclerosis complex, which is not indicated in the provided information.
A lipoma in the left ventricle could present as a smooth, mobile mass, though they are less common and the imaging characteristics might differ from those described.

rationales.F03: Left ventricular mass is a key feature of several cardiac tumors and thrombi.
rationales.F11: Mobile, smooth, oval, pedunculated mass is characteristic of myxoma.
rationales.F12: Focal contrast enhancement is consistent with myxoma or fibroelastoma.
